metadata.why_hard: The unconstrained Dyck grammar is easy; enforcing depth <= 3 and the parent rule needs depth-indexed nonterminals split by parent type, and CNF conversion must not break them. The language is regular (12-state minimal DFA) but a CFG answer is required.

prompt:
TASK: context-free grammar (in Chomsky normal form) for a constrained bracket language

Alphabet: the four symbols ( ) [ ] (round and square brackets).
A word is WELL-NESTED if its symbols can be paired so that every ( is paired with a later ), every [ with a later ], and pairs are properly nested (no crossing, as in ([)]). A paired opening and closing symbol together with everything between them is a GROUP; it is a (-group or a [-group according to its opening symbol. The DEPTH of a group is 1 plus the number of groups that strictly contain it, so top-level groups have depth 1. The PARENT of a group is the smallest group that strictly contains it; top-level groups have no parent.

L is the set of words w such that:
  (1) w is non-empty and well-nested;
  (2) no group has depth greater than 3;
  (3) no (-group has a [-group as its parent.
(-groups may appear at top level or with a (-group as parent. [-groups may have any parent, subject to (2).

Examples in L: (), [](), ([]), (([])), [[[]]]
Examples not in L: ε (empty), (] (not well-nested), [()] (a (-group whose parent is a [-group), [[()]] (same reason), (((()))) (depth 4)

Give a grammar in Chomsky normal form that generates exactly L.

WHAT TO SUBMIT
A context-free grammar in Chomsky normal form (CNF), as one JSON object with these keys:
  "start"       : the start nonterminal
  "productions" : list of objects {"lhs": <nonterminal>, "rhs": [<symbol>, ...]}, one object per alternative
Symbols: an rhs entry that is exactly one of the terminal symbols ( ) [ ] is a terminal; every other name is a nonterminal. Use names without spaces; uppercase names such as S, A1, X_2 are recommended.
CNF means every production has exactly one of these two forms:
  A -> B C   (rhs is a list of two nonterminals), or
  A -> t     (rhs is a list containing exactly one terminal).
Not allowed: ε-productions (empty rhs), unit productions A -> B, right-hand sides with three or more symbols, and mixed right-hand sides such as A -> t B. The start symbol may also appear on right-hand sides. A CNF grammar cannot generate ε, which is why L excludes ε.

HOW IT IS GRADED
1. The grammar must be in CNF exactly as defined above (otherwise score 0).
2. For EVERY word w over the alphabet with 1 <= |w| <= 16: the grammar must generate w if and only if w is in L. This is checked exhaustively by an exact algorithm, not by sampling.
3. The grammar must generate infinitely many words, because L is infinite.
Score: 1.0 if all three checks pass, otherwise 0. Equivalence of context-free grammars is undecidable in general, so the check is exact only for words up to length 16; your grammar should nevertheless generate exactly L.

FORMAT EXAMPLE (for an unrelated language { x^n y^n : n >= 1 } over {x, y})
```json
{"start": "S", "productions": [
  {"lhs": "S", "rhs": ["X", "Y"]}, {"lhs": "S", "rhs": ["X", "T"]},
  {"lhs": "T", "rhs": ["S", "Y"]},
  {"lhs": "X", "rhs": ["x"]}, {"lhs": "Y", "rhs": ["y"]}]}
```
title: Bounded-depth two-bracket Dyck variant (CNF grammar)
